t.7.72.1: After a short while, having heard of it, that divine sage of boundless splendor, surrounded by his disciples and tormented by hunger, returned to his own hermitage.
t.7.72.3: Anger arose in him, especially as he was tormented by hunger, and, as if burning up the three worlds, he spoke these words to his disciples.
t.7.72.2: He saw Arajā, wretched and covered with dust, like moonlight swallowed by the red glow of dawn, no longer shining at daybreak.
t.7.72.5: The destruction of this evil-minded, wicked-souled one, together with his followers, has arrived, he who wishes to touch the blazing flame of fire.
t.7.72.4: Behold the ruin, dreadful in aspect like a furious flame of fire, that comes upon the perverse Daṇḍa, who does not know himself.
t.7.72.6: Since he has committed such a sin, terrible to behold, that fool shall therefore reap the fruit of his wicked deed.
t.7.72.7: Within seven nights that evil-minded king, whose conduct is given to sinful deeds, will meet his death together with his servants, his army and his mounts.
t.7.72.8: And Pākaśāsana will burn up the realm of this evil-minded one, a hundred yojanas on every side, with a great rain of dust.
t.7.72.9: All the beings that are here, both the stationary and the moving, will be utterly destroyed by a great rain of dust.
t.7.72.10: As far as the realm of Daṇḍa extends, so far every towering thing will, after seven nights, be reduced as if to dust and vanish from sight.
t.7.72.11: Having spoken thus, burning with anger, he said to the people dwelling in the hermitage: "Go and dwell at the borders of the land."
t.7.72.12: Having heard the words of Uśanas, the people who dwelt in the hermitage went forth from his realm and then made their dwelling place outside it.
t.7.72.13: Having spoken thus to the company of sages, he said this to Arajā: "O foolish one, dwell right here in the hermitage, fully composed in mind."
t.7.72.14: O Arajā, free from distress, enjoy this lake of most lovely radiance, extending a full yojana, and let the time be awaited here.
t.7.72.15: But those beings who come to dwell near you on that night shall forever be safe from being slain by the rain of dust.
t.7.72.16: Having spoken thus, Bhārgava moved his dwelling elsewhere; and after seven days everything was reduced to ashes, just as the expounder of the Veda had declared.
t.7.72.17: That realm of his, the domain of Daṇḍa on the slopes of the Vindhya and Śaivala mountains, was cursed long ago by that brahmarṣi when an unrighteous deed had been committed.
t.7.72.18: From that time on, O Kākutstha, it has been called the Daṇḍaka forest; and the place where the ascetics dwelt then became Janasthāna.
t.7.72.19: All this that you ask me about has been told to you, O Rāghava. The time for performing the evening twilight worship is passing, O hero.
t.7.72.20: All these great sages, holding full water-pots, having performed their water rites, O tiger among men, stand all around worshipping the sun.
t.7.72.21: Honored by those sages, the foremost of brahmins gathered together, the sun has gone to its setting, Rāma. Go and touch water.
